title: What to order at Japanese restaurants and sushi shops when you want to lose weight
intro: Many people think all Japanese food is healthy. That's partly true, but there are also mayo-loaded rolls and fried dishes that are high in calories. If you choose well, a sushi shop can be a great place to eat for your goals. The calories below are estimates.

best.name: Salmon sashimi (5 pieces)
best.why: High protein with no rice. Rich in good fats and very filling.

best.name: Salmon or tuna nigiri (2 pieces)
best.why: Less rice, more fish. The simplest sushi choice.

best.name: Saba shioyaki or grilled fish (1 serving)
best.why: Fish grilled with salt. Packed with protein and no sweet sauce.

best.name: Chawanmushi (1 bowl)
best.why: Soft steamed egg. Light and tasty as a starter.

best.name: Edamame (1 plate)
best.why: A snack with protein and fibre. Good to munch on while waiting for your food.

best.name: Miso soup (1 bowl)
best.why: Warm and low in calories. Helps you feel fuller.

careful.name: Mixed tempura (1 set)
careful.why: Prawns and vegetables in fried batter. Share it or take just 2-3 pieces.

careful.name: Mentai roll or cheese roll (6 pieces)
careful.why: Mayo, cheese and sauce add a lot of calories. Choose plain maki or nigiri instead.

careful.name: Katsu don (1 bowl)
careful.why: Battered fried chicken on rice with sweet sauce. Consider grilled teriyaki or share it.

careful.name: Kani mayo salad (1 plate)
careful.why: Looks like a salad, but has lots of mayo. Take just a little.

careful.name: Takoyaki (6 pieces)
careful.why: Batter, sauce and mayo. Nice as a shared snack, not as a main meal.

hacks: Start with miso soup and edamame so you're not too hungry when the sushi arrives.
Pick more sashimi and nigiri than mayo-loaded rolls.
Ask for sauce and mayo on the side. Dip a little, don't pour.
At the conveyor belt counter, set a plate limit first, for example 5 plates, before you start picking.
For bento sets, choose grilled protein and ask for less rice.
drink: Hot or cold ocha with no sugar. Most sushi shops offer free ocha refills, so it's a perfect choice.

faq.q: Is it okay to eat sushi every week when losing weight?
faq.a: Yes, as long as you pick lighter options like sashimi, nigiri and plain maki. Watch the number of plates and the mayo rolls, because that's where calories add up easily.

faq.q: Japanese soy sauce is very salty. Should I worry?
faq.a: Soy sauce is high in sodium. Just dip a little, don't soak. Drink enough ocha or plain water throughout the meal.
